Downstream consumers expecting a per-modality breakdown may mis-handle duplicates.

threads.body: The docstring claims video/document inputs are detected, but _MIME_MODALITY only maps image/ and audio/, so a request with video/document parts will route to _multimodal_response without any corresponding modality entries in promptTokensDetails. Either extend _MIME_MODALITY to cover those MIME prefixes or narrow the docstring to match the supported modalities.

+def _response_modalities(body):
+    """Requested output modalities (defaults to TEXT)."""
+    cfg = body.get("generationConfig") or body.get("generation_config") or {}

+    return [str(m).upper() for m in mods] or ["TEXT"]

+def _has_inline_media(body):
+    """True if the request includes non-text media (image/audio/video/document) input."""
+    for content in body.get("contents") or []:
+        for part in content.get("parts") or []:
+            if any(key in part for key in ("inlineData", "inline_data", "fileData", "file_data")):
+                return True
+    return False

threads.body: `_has_audio` is true for audio input alone, so the audio-input-only request in `test_chat_reports_audio_tokens_for_audio_input` — whose `modalities` defaults to text-only — still reports 15 generated audio tokens. Real OpenAI reports generated audio tokens only alongside a populated `message.audio`, which this body also omits. Deriving the completion audio count and the audio message part from the requested output modality would keep the input/output split meaningful.
